matter_title: Petition for Writ of Certiorari for Quasi-judicial Proceeding
assignment_title: Legal Memorandum to Board of County Commissioners
prompt:
1st ASSIGNMENT
TO: Denise Swarek, Assistant County Attorney
FROM: Thomas Rowe, County Attorney
RE: PETER SPAHN, ET. AL., V. LEE COUNTY; Case No. 24-CA-1479
DATE: October 27, 2025
________________________________________
We received the attached Order Granting Petition for Writ of Certiorari.  
You are initially provided with the following record as uploaded files. Limit your review to these documents and what legal research is necessary to identify applicable rules and case law relevant to these documents. Do not conduct legal research beyond that. All legal analysis should be based on the versions of statutes, regulations, and ordinances in effect as of January 1, 2025.
•	Resolution Z-23-035 (Resolution.docx)
•	Petition for Writ of Certiorari (Petition.docx)
•	Order Granting Petition (Orderpdf.docx)
•	LCU Project Detail (LCU Project.pdf)
Review only these documents and draft a structured legal memorandum to the Board of County Commissioners that 1) outlines the Order and case history, 2) explains the implications of the Order, 3) identifies options and available actions for Lee County, 4) recommends a legal course of action to the Board. Use full Bluebook citation format.

rubric.criterion: States in the first assignment that the effect of the Order Granting Writ of Certiorari is that the Board's decision is overturned.
rubric.source:
Florida law is unequivocal that when a circuit court finds error in a local government’s quasi-judicial land use decision, its power is limited to quashing the decision and remanding the matter “as if no order had been entered.” See Broward County v. G.B.V. Int’l, Ltd., 787 So. 2d 838, 845 (Fla. 2001) (“When a circuit court grants certiorari relief, it quashes the order and leaves the matter pending before the lower tribunal as if no order had been entered.”).
https://caselaw.findlaw.com/court/fl-supreme-court/1495364.html#:~:text=When,judgment,-%2E
rubric.justification: This rubric item is requested directly in the following portion of the prompt: “Review only these documents and draft a legal memorandum to the Board of County Commissioners that . . .2) explains the implications of the Order.”

rubric.criterion: States in the first assignment that the county must stop construction activities as a result of the Order Granting Writ of Certiorari.
rubric.source:
LCU Project.pdf at 1 shows that construction has started.
"Construction of the Southeast Advanced Water Reclamation Facility started on October 6, 2025."
Injunctive relief is not an available remedy in a writ of certiorari of a quasi-judicial decision. See City of Fort Pierce v. Dickerson, 588 So.2d 1080, 1082 (Fla. 4th DCA 1991). https://www.casemine.com/judgement/us/59148822add7b049344ef125#:~:text=Since,injunction 
"Since review of the resolution should have been by certiorari, the trial court was without jurisdiction to entertain a complaint for declaratory and injunctive relief and should not have granted the Dickersons' motion for a temporary injunction."
rubric.justification: This rubric item is requested directly in the following portion of the prompt: “Review only these documents and draft a legal memorandum to the Board of County Commissioners that . . .2) explains the implications of the Order.”

rubric.criterion: States in the first assignment that the exclusive method of review of a quasi-judicial decision is by petition for writ of certiorari under Fla. R. App. P. 9.100(c) (2025) within 30 days of the written decision.
rubric.source:
Fla. R. App. P. 9.100(c) (2025); https://rules.floridaappellate.com/rule-9-100/#:~:text=Petitions,by%20certiorari
"Petitions for Certiorari; Review of NonFinal Agency Action; Review of Prisoner Disciplinary Action. The following shall be filed within 30 days of rendition of the order to be reviewed:

(1) a petition for certiorari;

(2) a petition to review quasi-judicial action of agencies, boards, and commissions of local government, which action is not directly appealable under any other provision of general law but may be subject to review by certiorari;"
See City of Fort Pierce v. Dickerson, 588 So.2d 1080, 1082 (Fla. 4th DCA 1991).
https://www.casemine.com/judgement/us/59148822add7b049344ef125#:~:text=Thus,relief
"Thus, we conclude that the resolution by the Ft. Pierce City Commission was quasi-judicial. Consequently, we agree with Ft. Pierce's assertion that since the resolution was a quasi-judicial decision rendered by the Commission, it was reviewable only by petition for writ of certiorari, and not by a complaint for declaratory and injunctive relief."
rubric.justification: This rubric item is implied, though not directly requested, in the following portion of the prompt: “Review only these documents and draft a legal memorandum to the Board of County Commissioners that . . .2) explains the implications of the Order.” This is important in responding to the prompt question about implications of the order because it explains why injunctive relief is not available in a writ of certiorari of a quasi-judicial decision.

rubric.criterion: States in the first assignment that the exclusive method of challenging the issuance of a development order that materially alters the use or density or intensity of use on a particular piece of property is by filing a petition for writ of certiorari under Fla. Stat. § 163.3215(4) (2025) within 30 days of rendition of the development order.
rubric.source:
Fla. Stat. 163.3215(4) (2025); https://www.leg.state.fl.us/Statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&URL=0100-0199/0163/Sections/0163.3215.html#:~:text=the%20sole,for%20certiorari
"the sole method by which an aggrieved and adversely affected party may challenge any decision of local government granting or denying an application for a development order, as defined in s. 163.3164, which materially alters the use or density or intensity of use on a particular piece of property, is by an appeal filed by a petition for writ of certiorari filed in circuit court no later than 30 days following rendition of a development order or other written decision of the local government, or when all local administrative appeals, if any, are exhausted, whichever occurs later. An action for injunctive or other relief may be joined with the petition for certiorari."
A challenge to issuance of a development order, which is an executive function, is a separate cause of action from appeal of a quasi-judicial decision.
rubric.justification: This rubric item is implied, though not directly requested, in the following portion of the prompt: “Review only these documents and draft a legal memorandum to the Board of County Commissioners that . . .2) explains the implications of the Order.” This is crucial because challenging a development order is the sole method to seek injunctive relief under Fla. Stat. 163.3215(4).

rubric.criterion: States in the first assignment that the County could take the position that the rezoning is not necessary because the county is not bound by its local zoning laws in carrying out a governmental function.
rubric.source:
See Sandra G. Smith, Immunity of State and State Related Activities from Local Municipal Zoning Regulations: Florida Focus, 28 Fla. L. Rev. 800 (1967).
Available at: https://scholarship.law.ufl.edu/flr/vol28/iss3/9 
https://scholarship.law.ufl.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=2881&context=flr
"The Fourth District Court of Appeal relied
on Nichols for the premise that in the performance of a governmental activity the county should not be subject to its own zoning restrictions. 2 In a 1978
decision Dade County was challenged by private property owners when it attempted to violate its own zoning restrictions by building a jail facility on
property reserved for another use under a comprehensive zoning ordinance. 28
The Third District Court of Appeal recognized a right under common law and under Florida law for "a governmental entity to place a governmental
facility without regard to a comprehensive zoning ordinance or its procedures."
The article quotes Metropolitan Dade County v. Parkway Towers Condominium Ass'n, 281 So. 2d 68
(Fla. 3d DCA 1973), a 3rd DCA case establishing immunity from zoning for governmental purposes. The case is not found publicly available, however the FL Supreme Court accepted, but then discharged), a petition for writ. Note that the FL Supreme Court expressed a "prospective opinion" that local governments "should" go through rezonings if not in compliance, this is dicta and not binding as the court upheld the district court's decision on immunity.  
Parkway Towers Con. Ass'n v. Metropolitan Dade Cnty., 295 So.2d 295 (Fla. 1974); https://law.justia.com/cases/florida/supreme-court/1974/44260-0.html#:~:text=Although,ordinances,-%2E
"Although we now consider our issuance of the writ of certiorari to have been improvident in this case, which results in our discharge thereof, it is nevertheless our view prospectively that zoning variations to accommodate county or municipal facility purposes should either have been anticipated in zoning ordinances before construction or operation of such facilities is commenced *296 or, if this has not been done, construction should not be undertaken thereof until after due modification or change therefor is made in existing zoning ordinances."

rubric.criterion: States in the first assignment that the County should cease construction activities at the subject property.
rubric.source:
LCU Project.pdf at 1 shows that construction has started, which means the county has spent time and money on design, permitting, procurement of contractors, etc. The facility is also necessary to serve increased demand for water and sewer service caused by population growth and has been planned since 2010 (LCU Project.pdf at 4.)
In a similar case, the FL Supreme Court declined to delay construction of a public project based on zoning.
See Parkway Towers Con. Ass'n v. Metropolitan Dade Cty., 295 So.2d 295 (Fla. 1974); https://law.justia.com/cases/florida/supreme-court/1974/44260-0.html#:~:text=This%20being,result
"In this case it appears that on at least two occasions public hearings were held by the Metro County Commission on the question whether the construction of the subject holding facility for prisoners and the work release facility should go forward in the absence of a waiver therefor in the zoning ordinance and in each instance it was agreed by the Commission the construction should proceed. This being so, we feel no useful or practical purpose would be served in interrupting and delaying the construction until a zoning change is effected retroactively to accommodate the Commission's expressly resolved purpose when considered in connection with the fact that no direct conflict of decisions appears. To interrupt the construction now would cause needless expense and damage with no prospect or likelihood that the Commission would reach a different final result."
